newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Heavy rain hampers Liberia voters census.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain hampers Liberia voters census.

text.p: Liberia launched a 10-day voter census despite torrential rain on Tuesday as a crucial step on the road to July 19 national elections to end seven years of civil war.

The tropical downpour in the coastal West African state disrupted the start of voter registration in the capital, witnesses said, but electoral officials were confident that they would complete the exercise in time for the presidential and parliamentary poll.

"The beginning of the registration marks the beginning of the actual electoral exercise. Rain or shine, you should see the process as a major opportunity to contribute to the restoration of peace in Liberia," commission chairman Henry Andrews in a statement.
The downpour stopped traffic in the capital Monrovia, arguably Africa's wettest, and only a few of the 600 voter registration centres there opened, registering only a handful of people.

The independent electoral commission said that despite the rain it would send more registrars to the jungle interior to prepare for the polls, part of a peace deal brokered by Liberia's West African neighbours last August.
Rain did not stop the head of the West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG from meeting presidential contenders following reports of campaign violence.

"ECOMOG will not allow political thuggery or violence during this campaign and election period," General Victor Malu said in a statement after reports of violence involving rival party supporters when the campaign opened on June 16.
The electoral commission says it has set up 2,000 registration centres across the country. Each will register up to 500 would-be voters, giving a projected electorate of about one million voters.

Warlords-turned-politicians Charles Taylor, Alhaji Kromah and George Boley are among a dozen candidates running for president. Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, charismatic former Africa director for the U.N. Development Programme, is standing against them.
Almost half of Liberia's pre-war population of 2.5 million fled during the war, launched by Taylor in 1989.

United Nations officials estimate that 667,000 are still outside the country, scattered among neighbours such as Ivory Coast and Guinea. Under the peace plan, only Liberians in Liberia are eligible to vote.
The war killed well over 150,00 people in the nation set up by freed American slaves in 1847.
